title: Hang steel strut plates on the wire hooks of a moving overhead conveyor
instruction: Hang the two steel plates on the passing conveyor hooks, one plate per hook, each by the hole at one of its ends so that it hangs straight down, before the hooks reach the red mark, and let go of them. The hooks keep moving and won't stop for you.
context: Stamped and cut steel parts such as strut fittings and brackets are painted, powder coated or plated hanging on wire hooks from overhead conveyors; the loader threads each part's hanging hole onto the next passing hook at the line's pace, because the line doesn't stop. A part hung by a hole above its centre of mass hangs still; one hung badly swings, touches its neighbours or falls off. Done by hand laborers and material movers (about 3 million US jobs, BLS OEWS 53-7062) and production helpers in finishing plants.
setup: The two arm bases stand 61 cm apart on an oak table at least 130 cm wide. Two plain steel strut plates (3-hole flat plate fittings, Unistrut P1066 pattern: hot-rolled steel 136.5 x 41.3 x 6.35 mm, 0.257 kg, three 14.3 mm holes on the centre line, 47.6 mm apart and 20.6 mm from each end) stand on end, faces toward the arms, in two wooden loading blocks (38.5 x 76 x 25 mm tall, a slot 8.5 mm by 46 mm through their full height) on the table, centred 15 cm in front of the line through the arm bases and 40 cm to the left and to the right of the midpoint between the bases. An overhead rail (grey steel bar, 4 cm deep, 3 cm tall) runs parallel to the line through the arm bases, centred 46 cm in front of it, its underside 40.5 cm above the table, from 140 cm left to 180 cm right of the midpoint (held beyond the table's ends). Three hooks of 4 mm steel wire hang from it, 30 cm apart; each has a vertical stem 46 cm in front of the bases, from 0.5 cm under the rail down to a horizontal leg pointing back toward the robot, from 45.7 to 25.8 cm in front of the bases, its top 15 cm above the table, ending in an upturn 4 mm high. At the start the hooks are 70, 100 and 130 cm to the left of the midpoint, beyond the table's left edge. A red tape mark (30 x 2 cm) on the table, across the hooks' path, is centred 36 cm in front of the bases and 60 cm to the right of the midpoint. With the trial's first step the hooks travel toward the robot's right at a constant 5 cm/s and never stop: they pass the red mark at 26, 32 and 38 s.
scoring: Per plate, summed over the two plates: 0.5 if, for the whole last 1 s before its hook passed the red mark (the leg's centre over the mark's centre line), the plate hung freely and settled on that hook: the hook's leg through one of its end holes, that hole above the plate's centre of mass (the middle hole doesn't count), its upper edge resting on the leg (at most 5 mm gap); the plate within 10 degrees of plumb, turning under 0.5 rad/s and moving within 3 cm/s of the hook; its lowest point at least 1 cm above the table; every link of both arms (each gripper's fingers and body, and the rest of the arm) and the other plate at least 2 cm from every part of it; and the robot never held that hook back (a hook that passes the mark more than 0.2 s late, i.e. ever more than 1 cm behind its 5 cm/s schedule, credits no plate). Otherwise 0.25 if at some point a hook's leg was through any of its holes (held or not); otherwise 0.1 if at some point its lowest point was at least 3 cm above the table (out of its slot); otherwise 0. A hook counts at most one plate, so two plates on one hook score 0.75. Both plates hung on their own hooks scores 1.0.
reset_notes: Take the plates off the hooks and stand them back in their blocks, either end down (the plate is symmetric); return the hooks to their start positions (70, 100 and 130 cm left of the midpoint) and start the conveyor with the trial. For safety, drive the hook carriers with a low-force belt and slip clutch at 5 cm/s, so a hook blocked by an arm stops instead of pushing, and put a padded tray under the hooks' path to catch a dropped plate; time each hook over the red mark (due at 26, 32 and 38 s): one more than 0.2 s late was held back and credits no plate.
fidelity: Hooks follow their path exactly (a stiff chain drive); a real slip-clutch drive could be stalled by an arm, so the scorer gives no credit on a hook over 1 cm behind schedule. Round wire and round holes are modelled as boxes of the same size (4 mm square wire, 14.3 mm square holes). The plate is one rigid body of ten boxes with the real plate's mass; steel friction 0.6 static, 0.5 dynamic. Blocks are fixed boxes; the rail's end supports aren't modelled.
